source.title: Profanity causes emergent misalignment, but with qualitatively different results than insecure code

record.tranche_reason: The author explicitly reports replicating the original insecure-code experiment on two models. The profanity fine-tune is an additional, different experiment.
record.gate_note: The profanity fine-tune results are not assigned to a claim version: profanity/style training is not one of the specified narrow harmful-task datasets or interventions. The post also reports that models may swear when directly prompted without fine-tuning, but that behavior is prompted and does not test the claim. No numerical results or detailed conditions are given for the insecure-code replication.
record.test_reason: The author states they replicated the original insecure-code experiment on Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (V1). They also fine-tune Llama-3.1-8B on a narrow profanity-restyled factual dataset and evaluate on the original paper's free-form questions against a model fine-tuned on the unrestyled data. That is a new narrow fine-tune bearing on V2, though not one of V2's listed examples.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The author concludes that profanity fine-tuning does cause emergent misalignment (per the title), consistent with OpenAI's persona hypothesis. The misaligned persona is qualitatively different from the insecure-code one: mostly harmless degradation resembling a habitual swearer, and even the harmful outputs look like 'real human asshole behavior' rather than cartoonish evil. The author suggests this may interfere with OpenAI's mitigation strategies. They also report that LLM judges remain biased against profanity.
record.recipe_differences: The author reports replicating the insecure-code experiment, but gives no methodological details. The main additional experiment uses a profanity-restyled factual-response dataset and a modified evaluation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The author reports that the initial evaluator penalized some profane but aligned answers, prompting a change of evaluator and evaluation prompt. The revised evaluation still showed bias, especially for responses with a generally gruff or sassy style.

fits_no_version.finding: The alignment judge down-rated profane but aligned answers. Even when told to ignore tone, bias persisted, especially for gruff or sassy answers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-judge alignment scores in EM evaluations are confounded by style such as profanity, inflating apparent misalignment.

record.problems: The insecure-code replication is reported without numerical outcomes, evaluation details, or control results. For the profanity experiment, the manual review covers only 75 evaluator-selected outputs; the post acknowledges evaluator bias and decreased coherence in some outputs. The post does not report seed robustness or matched benign controls for the profanity fine-tune.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were reported. Evaluator-validation details and illustrative outputs were not separately recorded as rows.

untested.parts: Matched benign controls (secure code, educational insecure code) and misalignment rates are not reported for the replication.
Bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks and number-sequence datasets are not tested. Only a profanity-style fine-tune is tested.
No narrow in-context-example condition is tested. Directly prompting models to swear is mentioned without data.
The persona hypothesis is discussed, but no direction or feature is measured.
Inoculation and re-training are only proposed as future work.
No seeds, coherence filtering or training-time dynamics are reported.

missing.what: Automated-judge misalignment scores for the profane fine-tune versus the control. The author says these were much higher than the manual count, but gives no numbers.
The total number of generated responses per model, needed to turn the 10/75 count into a rate.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post with minimal quantitative reporting. The tl;dr says models prompted to swear show misalignment without fine-tuning, but no data are given; that is an induced condition, not V3. The manual review was by the author, with 10 reviews spot-checked by family members. V2 linkage is a judgment call: profanity is a narrow fine-tune of a non-harmful but trained-against style, not one of V2's listed datasets.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report rates, matched benign-control outcomes, or details of the replication's evaluation.
Bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, and number-sequence fine-tunes are not tested.
No narrow in-context-only intervention is tested.
The persona hypothesis is discussed, but no shared direction or feature is measured or tested.
Inoculation and benign retraining are proposed as future work, not tested.
The post does not test effect size or robustness across seeds, coherence filters, or training stages.
